memory_update.text: COHR should remain a reference anchor for InP/compound-semiconductor optical capacity, but not the primary underfollowed alpha lane due to high attention and large-cap status.
ALMU is a speculative-shadow candidate for alternative III-V-on-silicon photonics; survival to later layers requires customer qualification, commercial revenue, and wafer-yield evidence.
AAOI has direct AI datacenter optical-transceiver order evidence and should be checked for customer concentration, margin conversion, and dependence on constrained optical components.
Fabrinet maps to the manufacturing-capacity layer of AI optical interconnects, not the InP wafer/device layer; it may benefit if OEMs outsource 800G/1.6T scale-up.

The strongest reference evidence points to constrained InP-linked photonics capacity at established optical suppliers, while the underfollowed lane centers on alternative III-V-on-silicon platforms, optical-engine suppliers, and contract manufacturers exposed to 800G/1.6T AI data-center demand.
